objective: Freeze the multi-scenario registry contract and ownership boundary as one machine-readable file plus an executable validator, before any registry implementation is written.
decision_supported: Whether Issue #300 may implement a Scenario Registry against this field list, and whether #311, #301, #302, #305 and #306 may add fields only by amending the contract in a reviewed change.
acceptance: the contract file declares required fields, optional fields, exact version matching, diagnostic codes, bounds, allowed adapters, forbidden field names and an ownership table
the detector imports the shared ActionType vocabulary instead of copying it, so a manifest cannot declare a private action vocabulary
a manifest that names joint, velocity, torque, CAN, controller-goal, trajectory or emergency-stop fields fails closed at any nesting depth
a manifest that declares a second policy or verifier implementation fails closed
an unknown field, unstable scenario_id, inexact scenario_version, unknown adapter and out-of-vocabulary evidence_status each fail with a stable diagnostic code
a duplicate scenario_id and scenario_version pair fails closed, and a distinct version is not a duplicate
the cleaning example declares clean_workspace as pending, reports NOT_EXECUTABLE, and is turned into a failure only by --require-executable
SCRIPTED_FIXTURE, NOT_EXECUTED and BLOCKED are non-release-eligible so a fixture is never rendered as physical success
the detector never imports the runtime, starts ROS or Gazebo, or writes a run or an event
the ADR is linked from tasks/README.md and both examples are committed non-executable manifests
evidence: pytest transcript for tests/unit/test_scenario_contract.py with the passed count
check_scenario_contract.py stdout showing PASS for the committed examples and FAIL for --require-executable
the contract file and both example manifests as committed artifacts
make contract, make scenario-check and make context-check output
stop_conditions: the change requires editing interfaces/json_schema/scenario.schema.json or the ScenarioManifest model, which is a separately approved follow-up
the change requires extending the shared ActionType vocabulary, which belongs to Issue #306
the change requires a new runtime dependency
a frozen scenario fixture would have to be renamed, re-seeded or re-hashed
data_classification: public repository documentation and contract test fixtures; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may draft the ADR, the contract file, the examples, the detector and the tests; a named human Owner accepts the contract boundary and any field addition
risks_and_fallbacks: the contract could over-specify fields that #300 does not need; fallback is that #300 amends the contract file in a reviewed change and adds one test per new field
a forbidden-field name list is a denylist and cannot be exhaustive; fallback is that the ownership table routes authority away from manifests so a missed name grants no authority
the cleaning example could be read as a claim that cleaning exists; fallback is evidence_status NOT_EXECUTED, the SCENARIO_PENDING_ACTION notice and the explicit non_goals entries
rollback is a single revert of this commit; no runtime, schema, fixture or hardware path is touched
